skill.name: unmerge
skill.description: Split a flat image (PNG, JPG or WebP) into separate transparent PNG layers with Unmerge, with the hidden parts behind objects filled in. Use when the user wants to separate an image into layers, pull a subject or text off its background as its own layer, make an editable layered version of a poster, illustration or screenshot, or "unflatten" an image. Needs an Unmerge API key in UNMERGE_API_KEY.
skill.summary: Separate flat images into named PNG layers with canvas positions and reconstructed hidden areas through the Unmerge service.
skill.author: Unmerge

content.user_title: Split Flat Images into Editable PNG Layers
content.value_statement: Flat images combine subjects, text, and backgrounds, making separate edits difficult. This skill guides Unmerge processing to return positioned PNG layers with reconstructed hidden areas.
actual_capabilities: Submit PNG, JPG, or WebP images through connected Unmerge MCP tools or the HTTP API.
Request specific subjects, text, or backgrounds using a plain-language separation prompt.
Retrieve named PNG layers with canvas bounds, stacking order, and temporary download links.
Use Unmerge to reconstruct hidden image areas behind separated objects.
Poll project status and retrieve fresh layer links after existing links expire.
Check credits, explain additional charges, and unlock pending layers only with user agreement.
limitations: Requires an Unmerge API key, internet access, and available service credits; selected images leave the local environment.
Accepts PNG, JPG, and WebP images up to 10 MB and 4 megapixels, with at most 17 returned layers.
Costs one credit per returned layer and requires at least five credits to start a split.
Provides PNG layers rather than a native layered document; download links expire after one hour.

use_cases.title: Prepare poster elements for redesign
use_cases.description: Separate a poster title, subject, and background into positioned PNG layers for later editing.

use_cases.title: Extract campaign image subjects
use_cases.description: Isolate a requested subject from campaign artwork and retrieve the returned layer files.

use_cases.title: Recover movable illustration elements
use_cases.description: Separate a flattened illustration into named elements with reconstructed hidden areas and stacking metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Split a first image
prompt_templates.prompt: Split my attached image into layers with Unmerge. Check my credits before starting and provide the returned PNG links.

prompt_templates.title: Choose specific elements
prompt_templates.prompt: Separate the title, person, and background in my poster. Include each returned layer's name, canvas bounds, and stacking order.

prompt_templates.title: Finish a pending project
prompt_templates.prompt: Check Unmerge project [project ID]. Wait between polls, refresh expired download links, and ask before unlocking layers that require additional credits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: manage project status and additional charges.

prompt_templates.title: Process a controlled batch
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare these images for Unmerge processing. Check format, size, pixels, and credits, then explain expected costs and wait for my approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review a batch before submission.

output_examples.input: Show an example result for separating a poster title, person, and background.
output: Example layer names: Background, Person, and Title.
Each returned layer includes a PNG link, canvas bounds, and stacking order.
Download links remain valid for one hour.

output_examples.input: My project reports that more credits are needed. What happens next?
output: The project needs additional credits before its layers can be unlocked.
I will report the amount owed and wait for your approval before unlocking.

best_practices: Use only images you may share with Unmerge, and keep your API key out of messages and files.
Check credits before batches and approve any additional unlock charges explicitly.
Reuse the same idempotency key for retries and download desired layers before their links expire.
anti_patterns: Uploading confidential images without authorization to use an external processing service.
Retrying an HTTP submission with a new idempotency key and unintentionally creating duplicate splits.
Assuming PNG layers preserve native text, vectors, or a complete layered editor document.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when the required MCP tools or HTTP access are available.

faq.question: Do I need an Unmerge account and API key?
faq.answer: Yes. Obtain an Unmerge API key, configure UNMERGE_API_KEY, and ensure your account has enough credits.

faq.question: Which image formats and sizes are supported?
faq.answer: Use PNG, JPG, or WebP images up to 10 MB and 4 megapixels.

faq.question: How much does a split cost?
faq.answer: Each returned layer costs one credit, with at most 17 layers. At least five credits are required to start.

faq.question: Does the skill process images locally?
faq.answer: No. It submits selected images to the external Unmerge service through MCP tools or its HTTPS API.

faq.question: What files and download links will I receive?
faq.answer: You receive named PNG layers with canvas positions and stacking order. Links expire after one hour; retrieving the project provides fresh links.
